.qc-cache/coldwater-strict-2026-10-02-r12/task/tests/scored/{functional,polish,visual}/judge.toml (headers, [scoring], criterion descriptions searched for cross-criterion or stop-on-failure wording)
evidence: All three scored dimensions are mode = "batched" and each prompt carries an explicit score-independently-and-continue instruction. tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:11 "Score each criterion independently and continue after any failure; return a verdict for every criterion. A failed criterion never ends the session.", reinforced by :10 "Never carry a verdict across criteria... a failure in one must not fail another whose own steps passed" and :26 "give every criterion its own verdict". tests/scored/polish/prompt.md:10 has the same sentence, plus :11 "Never carry a verdict across criteria". tests/scored/visual/prompt.md:13 "Score each criterion independently and continue after any failure or low score; return a score for every criterion... never carry a score across criteria." No scored prompt tells the judge to stop at the first failure. The only stop wording is scoped to one criterion and explicitly continues: functional/prompt.md:15 "after two failed attempts at the same control or step, stop and fail that criterion, then continue with the rest"; the tool-error rules (functional :27, polish :20, visual :21) likewise say "fail that criterion and move on". The out-of-budget rule (functional :12) fails only unattempted criteria. tests/app_context.md, injected into every prompt, agrees: "Criteria that do not depend on Run are still scored on their own steps; a criterion whose steps need a working Run fails if Run does not work." A search of the 42 functional, 6 polish and 3 visual criterion descriptions found no reference to another criterion's id or verdict and no instruction to fail the remaining criteria. The one all-or-nothing rule, "Global browser gate... If the gate fails, assign 0 to every criterion in this dimension" (line 5 of each scored prompt), is template wording (template functional/prompt.md:9-13, polish :8-12, visual :16-20), is a load/typing precondition and not a criterion miss, so it is not a row-38 defect. Gate dimensions (render, constraints: aggregation = "all_pass") are exempt. Counterexamples tried: a broken app whose Run never works still gets its Run-independent editor and persistence criteria scored separately per app_context; a conforming app that misses one criterion is not zeroed elsewhere by any prompt wording. Limits: this is a source reading. The private check-batched-independence-wording.py was not executed, and no configured judge run exists for these bytes, so judge compliance with the wording is unmeasured here; the hosted run in the evidence index is on an earlier candidate and is not relied on.
